name: The Chorus
summary: The cosmic pantheon of Vaeloria, called the Chorus for the song of creation the gods left behind. The Chorus is one truth; each species worships it through its own choir. Some gods are shared across species by the same name, some are the same being under different names, and some are unique to a single species.

deities.name: Solvane
deities.clergy: High temples called Halos; judges and reeves swear on his name.
deities.temperament: stern, lawful, merciful to the honest
deities.attitude_to_magic: Magic is a duty to be bound by law, not a gift.

worship_by_species.name: Solvane
worship_by_species.note: The canonical face of the Chorus; oaths, courts, and coronations fall to him.

worship_by_species.name: Aurel, the Far King
worship_by_species.note: The day that does not reach the deep groves. Worshipped politely at grove-edges, never at the heart.

worship_by_species.name: the Bright One Above
worship_by_species.note: A foreigner's god, a lamp for the surface. The deep-folk nod to him at sunrise and go back below.

worship_by_species.name: Ishmet, the Burning Crown
worship_by_species.note: In the desert the sun is a tyrant. Prayer to Ishmet is defensive: offerings against the burn, vows for mercy, never joy.

deities.name: Luneth
deities.symbol: a crescent over a full circle
deities.clergy: Moonwardens; they keep calendars, debts, and birthings.
deities.attitude_to_magic: The Glimmer waxes and wanes like her; it is not evil, but it is not to be trusted at full.

worship_by_species.name: Luneth
worship_by_species.note: Moonwardens reckon debts and births by her phases.

worship_by_species.name: Aelune, the Silver Mother
worship_by_species.note: Keeper of the grove-calendars; elven rites are timed to her marks.

worship_by_species.name: Erethat, the Deep Tide
worship_by_species.note: Not a moon to the deep-folk but the slow pulse of the earth — the rhythm that swells and falls in the deep places.

worship_by_species.name: the Pale Thief
worship_by_species.note: The desert moon steals heat. The hollowborn do not worship Luneth; they fear the Pale Thief who walks the night cold.

deities.name: Orbren
deities.symbol: a hammer over a broken ring
deities.clergy: Deep-Shaper priests; artisans, miners, and masons.
deities.attitude_to_magic: Hates the Glimmer; calls it a lie the earth never made.

worship_by_species.name: Orbren
worship_by_species.note: Patron of smiths, masons, and honest craft.

worship_by_species.name: Orbren
worship_by_species.note: The forge-god is the one deity every species names the same. To the deep-folk he is the first hammer, and every hall is his altar.

worship_by_species.name: the Stone-Hammer
worship_by_species.note: The green sees him as the one who cuts roots to raise stone. Necessary, respected, never loved.

worship_by_species.name: absent
worship_by_species.relation: known only as a northern god
worship_by_species.note: The sands hold no forges; his name is a rumor travelers bring from the Stone Crown.

deities.name: Veyra
deities.clergy: Verdant kin; druids of the old greenwood.
deities.temperament: wild, nurturing, unforgiving to harmers of green
deities.attitude_to_magic: The Glimmer is a sickness on living things; she purges it where it takes root.

worship_by_species.name: Veyra
worship_by_species.note: Worshipped at field-festivals and harvests.

worship_by_species.name: Veyra, the First Root
worship_by_species.note: To the greenfolk she is the only true god; the rest of the Chorus are lesser voices echoing her song.

worship_by_species.name: the Root-Rival
worship_by_species.note: The green that eats into mines and collapses shafts. The deep-folk placate her, never pray to her.

worship_by_species.name: rejected, the slow flood
worship_by_species.note: In the desert green is a rare mercy or a false promise; Veyra's name is said only with suspicion.

deities.name: Vaelmarr
deities.symbol: a wave breaking over a blade
deities.attitude_to_magic: Claims the Glimmer as his weapon when battle demands it — and damns those who refuse it.

worship_by_species.name: Vaelmarr
worship_by_species.note: God of sailors and soldiers; Storm-Bound bless fleets and warbands.

worship_by_species.name: Shardstorm
worship_by_species.note: No sea in the desert — he is the glass-storm that scours the dunes and gives rain only to the deserving. Their war-god.

worship_by_species.name: the Falling Sky
worship_by_species.note: The sea is a ceiling falling; the deep-folk find his tempests amusing and keep to their halls.

worship_by_species.name: the Young Storm
worship_by_species.note: The Greenwood is older than storms; the greenfolk do not deny him, they simply do not wait on him.

deities.name: Mornath
deities.clergy: Veil-keepers; funeral rites and last vows.
deities.attitude_to_magic: The Glimmer thins the Veil he guards; he is the first to fear it.

worship_by_species.name: Mornath
worship_by_species.note: Veil-keepers tend the dead and keep the Stilleven vigil.

worship_by_species.name: Karveth, the Still-Singer
worship_by_species.note: The finisher of halls; where humans fear him, the deep-folk toast him — every hall must be ended well.

worship_by_species.name: Elveth, the Long Sleep
worship_by_species.note: The autumn of the very old. The greenfolk sing him, not mourn him.

worship_by_species.name: the Hollow Mouth
worship_by_species.note: Buried cities ring the desert; death is a neighbor. Their rites are silence, and the Hollow Sign is his language.

deities.name: Ithyn
deities.clergy: The remembered few; scholars of the banned. Often hunted.
deities.attitude_to_magic: The Glimmer is a language to be relearned, not a sin.

worship_by_species.name: Ithyn
worship_by_species.note: His cult is heretical in the Crownlands but persists in the Hollow Mile and the Ashlands.

worship_by_species.name: the Whisperer
worship_by_species.note: The voice of the Quiet, the wound. Naming him is near-blasphemy in the Greenwood.

worship_by_species.name: rejected
worship_by_species.note: The deep-folk keep their own keeper of the forgotten and refuse Ithyn's open eye.

worship_by_species.name: the Under-Sands
worship_by_species.note: A buried eye under the dunes. The Rememberers of the sands dig old writing and trade it — they are the one cult that still openly keeps him, in silence.

deities.name: Cayren
deities.attitude_to_magic: The Glimmer is the best joke in the world; he delights in its chaos.

worship_by_species.name: Cayren
worship_by_species.note: Road-Singers bless travelers, gamblers, and the unlucky.

worship_by_species.name: Vess, the Turning Leaf
worship_by_species.note: Not a trickster to the green — change is the turning of the season, natural and inevitable.

worship_by_species.name: Dhar, the Shifting Dune
worship_by_species.note: The god of caravans, mirages, and the luck of the road. Every hollowborn caravan lights a candle for Dhar at dusk.

worship_by_species.name: rejected, a shallow voice
worship_by_species.note: The deep-folk do not deny Cayren exists; they simply will not name a noise of the surface.

species_unique_deities.name: Khord
species_unique_deities.clergy: Door-Keepers who seal the Sunken Halls and tend shafts that must not be reopened.
species_unique_deities.note: Not of the Chorus. Khord holds everything the earth has swallowed — and decides what stays buried. The deep-folk keep his door shut over all others.

species_unique_deities.name: the Eldertree
species_unique_deities.symbol: a five-stemmed leaf over a single root
species_unique_deities.clergy: the Root-Wardens, who guard the innermost grove where no stranger walks.
species_unique_deities.note: The first tree of creation, given its own soul when Veyra poured herself into the green. The greenfolk worship it as the eldest living thing, distinct from — but born of — Veyra.

species_unique_deities.name: Akhmat
species_unique_deities.symbol: a still pool under a ring of reeds
species_unique_deities.clergy: Well-Sisters who keep the deep wells and the spring-oases.
species_unique_deities.temperament: gentle, stubborn, unforgiving to those who poison water
species_unique_deities.note: The one merciful face in the desert pantheon. She is said to weep springs; her wells must never be fouled, or she turns them to salt.

species_overview.note: The base canon; the Chorus as written. Regional kingdoms vary the emphasis but not the names.

species_overview.pantheon: Orbren (chief), Erethat, Karveth; tolerated: the Bright One Above
species_overview.note: The deep-folk keep a closed choir: forge, deep tide, and the ending of halls. Anything of the surface is either foreign or refused.
The greenfolk hold Veyra as the only true god and the rest as lesser voices. Ithyn is unnameable; the Glimmer is their great fear.

species_overview.pantheon: Ishmet, Shardstorm, the Hollow Mouth, Dhar; secret: the Under-Sands
species_overview.note: A harsh, defensive pantheon: appeasement, silence, and luck. They are the only species to keep Ithyn's cult alive, in the dark.

worship_notes: The theological truth is one Chorus; the species choirs are arrangements of the same song. Human clergy call the other names heresy; the deep-folk say the surface mishears the rhythm.
Luneth is the sharpest fault-line: a beloved mother to humans and elves, a deep pulse to dwarves, a demon to the hollowborn.
Since the Sundering no god is universally worshipped; the Chorus is honored as a whole at high festivals.
Ithyn's cult is outlawed in the Crownlands but persists in the Hollow Mile, the Ashlands, and among the hollowborn Rememberers.
The Censer order claims to serve no god, only the containment of the Glimmer — many suspect they answer to Mornath.
